title: Fundamentals of Materials Science and Engineering
description: Fundamental principles of materials science and engineering and their application toward complex engineering challenges; relationship between materials structure and structural and functional properties of engineered materials; property-performance relationships; principle classes of materials, as illustrated through key materials advances; current directions in the field.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CHEM 107 or CHEM 119 and PHYS 206 .

title: Materials in Society
description: Introduction to the study and practice of materials science and engineering; current topics in materials research and development, focusing on the impact of advanced materials on engineering fields and society; application of scientific engineering principals to guiding materials engineering process, with examples drawn from real-life case studies.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 201 , or concurrent enrollment; or approval of instructor.

title: Thermodynamics of Materials
description: Basic concepts and fundamental laws of thermodynamics; processes and thermodynamic engines; phase equilibria and phase diagrams of simple substances; chemical reactions of condensed phases; computational software for thermodynamic and phase diagram calculations.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 201 , AERO 413 , BMEN 343 , CHEN 322 , CVEN 306 , MEEN 222/MSEN 222 , MMET 206 , MSEN 222/MEEN 222 , or NUEN 265 , or concurrent enrollment; grade of C or better in MATH 152 or concurrent enrollment.

title: Materials Science
description: Mechanical, optical, thermal, magnetic and electrical properties of solids; differences in properties of metals, polymers, ceramics and composite materials in terms of bonding and crystal structure.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CHEM 107 or CHEM 119 ; grade of C or better in PHYS 206 . Cross Listing: MEEN 222/MSEN 222 .

title: Soft Matter
description: Structure, properties and function of various classes of soft matter including colloids, polymers, amphiphiles, liquid crystals and biomacromolecules; basic concepts of viscoelasticity, glass transition, liquid-liquid and liquid-solid transitions and gelation; forces acting between mesoscopic objects; supramolecular self-assembly in soft condensed matter.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CHEM 120 ; MSEN 201 , or concurrent enrollment.

title: Structure of Materials
description: Materials structure over many orders of scale; structure of non-crystalline materials; symmetry, unit cell and the atomic structure of crystalline materials; liquid crystals; structural defects in ordered solids; microstructures and hierarchical structures.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 201 , AERO 413 , BMEN 343 , CHEN 322 , CVEN 306 , MEEN 222/MSEN 222 , MMET 206 , MSEN 222/MEEN 222 , or NUEN 265 , or concurrent enrollment.

title: Materials Science and Engineering Seminar
description: Seminar series showcasing current advances in materials science and engineering and their application to solving real-world challenges, delivered by external speakers from industry, national laboratories, government R&D and alumni; emphasizes state-of-the-art technologies, career pathways, life-long learning, professional ethical considerations, hiring expectations and professional communication, with students engaging in Q&A and reflective summaries to synthesize emerging trends.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 201 , or concurrent enrollment.

title: Directed Studies
description: Directed study of selected problems in the area of materials science and engineering. May be taken for credit 4 times.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Approval of instructor.
repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

title: Special Topics In...
description: Selected topics in an identified area of materials science and engineering. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Approval of instructor.

title: Research
description: Research conducted under the direction of faculty member in materials science and engineering. May be taken three times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Freshman or sophomore classification and approval of instructor.
repeatability: May be taken three times for credit.

title: Unified Materials Lab I
description: Integration of materials synthesis, structural characterization and property evaluation; theory and practice of experimental and simulation techniques; emphasis on relationship between processing parameters and resulting materials structure.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 210 and MSEN 260 , or concurrent enrollment.

title: Unified Materials Lab II
description: Integration of materials synthesis, structural characterization and property evaluation; theory and practice of experimental and simulation techniques; emphasis on relationship between materials structure and resulting material's physical properties. Effective communication of experimental data and results; emphasis on written laboratory reports; engineering drawings and modern computer-aided design (CAD) tools.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 301 and MSEN 380 ; grade of C or better in MSEN 320 , or concurrent enrollment.

title: Kinetics of Materials
description: Presentation of physical principles that drive evolution of materials that are not in thermodynamic equilibrium; covers reaction kinetics and transport by diffusion; applies fundamental principles to analysis of materials phenomena, such as nuclear decay, surface reactions, interdiffusion, nucleation and growth, and solidification.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 210 .

title: Deformation and Failure Mechanisms in Engineering Materials
description: Survey of deformation and failure mechanisms in different materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers and composites; effect of atomistic structure, defects and microstructure on deformation and failure; deformation and failure mechanism maps and effects of temperature and deformation rate.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 260 .

title: Properties of Functional Materials
description: Origins of functional materials properties from their electronic and molecular structure; elementary quantum physics; modern theory of solids; dielectric, optical and magnetic properties of materials; current applications of functional materials.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 260 .

title: Numerical Methods for Materials Scientists and Engineers
description: Computing platforms addressing scientific/engineering problems related to materials science and engineering; analyze data; implement mathematical models of materials behavior; numerical methods to solve materials-related problems.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MATH 307 , MSEN 305 , and MSEN 320 .

title: Materials Characterization
description: Principles and techniques used in characterization of different materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, composites and semiconductor systems; microstructural, chemical/compositional and surface analysis methods; interpretation and analysis of the characterization results.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 250 and MSEN 260 .

title: Communicating Materials Science and Engineering
description: Effective communication of technical topics in materials science and engineering to technical and non-technical audiences; emphasis on written reports.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 301 , or concurrent enrollment.

title: High Impact Professional Development
description: Student participation in an approved high-impact learning practice; reflection on professional outcomes from engineering body of knowledge; documentation and self-assessment of learning experience at mid-curriculum point.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 205 and MSEN 281 ; junior or senior classification.

title: Design and Analysis of Materials Experiments
description: Systematic design of experimental investigations; team approach to identification of topics and development of experiment designs including establishing the need, associated requirements and objective; conduction of experiments; characterization of materials; analysis and interpretation of results; documentation of the procedures, analysis, results and conclusions; presentation of written and oral reports.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 301 ; grade of C or better in MSEN 302 or concurrent enrollment.

title: Materials Design I
description: Design process; need definition, functional analysis, performance requirements, evaluation criteria, conceptual design evaluation; introduction to systems engineering; parametric and risk analysis, failure analysis, material selection and manufacturability; cost and life cycle issues, project management; industry-relevant design projects.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 281 , MSEN 205 and MSEN 400 .

title: Materials Design II
description: Development of innovative solutions to industry-relevant design challenges; structured framework and methodology for design activities; innovation, computational materials science, synthesis and processing and analysis and characterization of material components; project definition, management, customer interaction and effective team participation; presentations and design reviews.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 401 .

title: Quantum Mechanics for Materials Scientists
description: Provides a background in quantum mechanics for students with little or no quantum mechanics background. The following topics will be covered: limits of classical physics, waves and quantum mechanics, physical interpretation of quantum theory, time-dependent Schrödinger equation and its applications, functions and operators, approximation methods, time-dependent perturbation theory, angular momentum, hydrogenic atom, quantum mechanics in crystalline materials, spin and quantum statistics.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in PHYS 207 and MSEN 330 ; or approval of instructor.

title: Field Theories in Materials Science
description: Introduce a range of field theory concepts for quantifying material behaviors; a comprehensive generic treatment of field theories for continuous media; concepts of fields and field variables beginning with transportable quantities (mass, electric charge, momentum, energy, etc.) and their balance equations; constitutive relations (notably for elasticity, electromagnetism, diffusion and other transport phenomena); linear response theory for examples such as Maxwell’s equations, deformation and motion of a continuum.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 320 or AERO 306 ; or approval of instructor.

title: Materials Processing
description: Synthesis, properties and processing of technologically important materials, metals, ceramics and polymers; thermodynamics and kinetics of different materials processing methods, casting, deformation processing, heat treatments, powder processing and sintering, coating, thin films processing, etc.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 250 , MSEN 305 , and MSEN 320 ; junior or senior classification.

title: Defects in Solids
description: Overview of point, line and surface defects in solids; relates defect properties to material behaviors, such as diffusion, plastic deformation or phase transformations; focuses on atomic defects in crystals, with additional examples from liquid crystals, superconductors or ferromagnets; incorporates atomistic modeling to examine defect structure.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 260 ; junior or senior classification; or approval of instructor.

title: Composites Processing and Performance
description: Fundamental science and design of composites; processing and design interaction about multiphase composites; processing science, experimental characterization, laminate analysis; design structure and processing.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 320 or MEEN 360 .

title: Polymer Science
description: Types of polymerization; molecular characteristics of polymer chains; single chain statistics and rubber elasticity; phase transitions, glass transition, viscoelasticity and time-temperature superposition; polymer structure at the molecular, microscopic and macroscopic level; polymer thermosets, thermoplastics, elastomers, fibers, and advanced nanoparticle-filled composites.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in PHYS 206 and CHEM 120 ; junior or senior classification; or approval of instructor.

title: Polymer Laboratories
description: Laboratory to prepare those interested in polymer research with necessary experimental and analytical skills to conduct and analyze experimental work.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 250 , junior or senior classification; or approval of instructor.

title: Nanomaterials Science
description: Nanotechnology and nanomaterials; types, fabrication, characterization methods and applications; current roles in technology and future impact of such systems on industry targeting.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 260 , junior or senior classification; or approval of instructor.

title: Processing and Patterning of Polymers
description: Fundamental and practical aspects in processing and patterning of polymers; melt processing, reaction processing, coatings, additive manufacturing and microfabrication. Emphasis will be placed on the use of polymer processing techniques in additive manufacturing and microfabrication.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 250 or BMEN 482 .

title: Materials Electrochemistry and Corrosion
description: Survey of thermodynamic and kinetic fundamentals of electrochemistry; multiscale materials corrosion mechanisms; details of interfacial aqueous electrochemical mechanisms and the environmental effects when materials are exposed to different conditions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 201 , AERO 413 , BMEN 344 , CHEN 322 , CVEN 306 , MEEN 222/MSEN 222 , MMET 207 , MSEN 222/MEEN 222 , or NUEN 265 ; or approval of instructor.

title: Corrosion and Electrochemistry Lab
description: Laboratory practice and principles for corrosion and electrochemistry methods; design, carry out and analyze a series of labs illustrating the most important techniques in the field; builds to an open-ended corrosion engineering problem resulting in preparation of a technical report for a hypothetical client.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 440 , or approval of instructor.

title: Corrosion Prevention and Control Methods
description: Cathodic protection and coatings; functional engineering approach to controlling and preventing aqueous corrosion; impressed current, galvanic anodes, organic, inorganic and hybrid coatings; case studies in oil and gas, energy, automotive and different industries.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 440 , or approval of instructor.

title: Failure Analysis in Materials Science and Engineering
description: Discussion and analysis of failure of engineering systems in terms of design, manufacturing, and service environments; broad background to common mechanisms of material failures in mechanical, electrical and chemical applications; emphasis on case studies and specific engineering disasters.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 320 ; or approval of instructor.

title: Fundamentals of Ceramics
description: Structure-property relationships of ceramics and ceramic composites; atomic bonding in ceramics; crystalline and glassy structures; phase equilibria and ceramic reactions; mechanical, electrical, thermal, dielectric, magnetic and optical properties; ceramic processing; different properties of ceramics will be related to their underlying structure.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 260 ; junior or senior classification; or approval of instructor.

title: Advanced Electronic Properties
description: Origins of electronic and optical (e-o) materials properties from their electronic and molecular structure; electron theory in solids; electronic transport and dielectric behavior; optical properties; tensor response; e-o material synthesis and characterization; e-o device applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 325 or ECEN 370 ; or approval of instructor.

title: Fabrication and Characterization of Electronic Materials
description: Properties, processing, and characterization of electronic materials; fabrication of semiconductors, patterning and etching of electronic and optical films; characterization of film structure, morphology, composition, and electronic and optical properties through different material analysis methods.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 325 or ECEN 370 .

title: Synthesis and Characterization of Electronic Materials
description: Properties, processing and characterization of electronic materials; synthesis of semiconductors and approaches to tailor specific electronic properties in electronically active materials; patterning and etching of electronic and optical films; characterization of film structure, morphology, composition and electronic and optical properties.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 325 or ECEN 370 , or approval of instructor.

title: Computational Materials Science and Engineering
description: Modern methods of computational modeling and simulation of materials properties and phenomena, including synthesis, characterization and processing of materials, structures and devices; quantum, classical and statistical mechanical methods, including semi-empirical atomic and molecular-scale simulations and other modeling techniques using macroscopic input.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MATH 307 , MSEN 305 , and MSEN 320 .

title: Atomistic Simulation of Materials
description: Modern methods of computational modeling and simulation of materials properties and phenomena at the atomistic scale; quantum, classical and statistical mechanical methods, including semi-empirical atomic and molecular-scale simulations, and other modeling techniques using macroscopic input.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 470 , or approval of instructor.

title: Internship
description: Practical experience working in a professional materials science and engineering setting offered on an individual basis. Must be taken on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory basis.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification and approval of instructor.

title: Directed Studies
description: Directed study of selected problems in the area of materials science and engineering. May be taken four times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Grade of C or better in MSEN 301 .
repeatability: May be taken four times for credit.

title: Special Topics In...
description: Selected topics in an identified area of materials science and engineering. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Approval of instructor.

title: Research
description: Research conducted under the direction of a faculty member in materials science and engineering. May be taken four times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MSEN 301 .
repeatability: May be taken four times for credit.
